title: Cellular automaton behavior falls into four basic classes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cellular automaton behavior falls into four basic classes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Despite differing in detail for almost every rule, the patterns produced by cellular automata of all kinds from random initial conditions can almost always be easily assigned to one of just four classes: uniform final state (class 1), simple stable or periodic structures (class 2), apparently random behavior (class 3), and interacting localized structures (class 4).

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: among all kinds of cellular automata, it seems that the patterns which arise can almost always be assigned quite easily to one of just four basic classes illustrated below.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “Four Classes of Behavior” (from p. 231), p. 231. Scope: all kinds of cellular automata evolved from random initial conditions

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing catalogs make the taxonomy testable for broad bounded samples, but class assignment requires interpretation and can vary with initial condition and run length. The universal scope cannot be exhaustively covered.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Create blinded classifications of long runs from random initial conditions using explicit metrics for convergence, periodicity, entropy, and localized structures. Measure agreement and the fraction of sampled rules that fit exactly one of four classes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Finite observations can hide long transients.

“All kinds” has no finite sampling frame.

The classes are visually and informally defined.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.46
data existence: 0.95
analysis feasibility: 0.82
discriminating power: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The 256 elementary rules are a complete public family and can be classified in days, so the four-way picture is testable on the space the chapter mostly shows. Almost always and all kinds extend past that space, and the text already records borderline rules that one definition places in one class and another definition places elsewhere. A sample can measure agreement; it cannot make the four bins unique or universal.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Evolve every elementary rule, and a declared sample of larger rules, from random initial conditions, and assign each run by pre-registered measurements of activity, damage spread, and localized structures. A large residue that fits none of the four bins, or a stable three-bin or five-bin partition with higher agreement, would challenge the four-class claim inside that sample.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Visual assignment is only partly reproduced by formal proxies.

The book itself exhibits rules that sit on class boundaries.

All kinds supplies no measure over dimension, radius, and number of states.
